query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Both files go in `/etc/systemd/system/`. That directory holds units you add yourself, and it takes precedence over the units packages install under `/usr/lib/systemd/system/`.

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.service`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup

# Hardening. ProtectSystem=strict makes the whole filesystem read-only,
# so list every path the backup writes to in ReadWritePaths=.
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/nightly-backup
StateDirectory=nightly-backup
```

**`/etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.timer`**

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly backup at 02:00

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true
AccuracySec=1min

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

To install and check them:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer
systemctl list-timers nightly-backup.timer
```

Only enable the timer. It starts the service when it fires, so the service needs no `[Install]` section.

A few choices to check against your script:

- **Write paths:** `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/nightly-backup` is a placeholder because I don't know where your backup writes. Replace it with the backup's real destination and any lock or log paths. Each of those paths must exist before the unit starts, or the unit fails with "Failed to set up mount namespacing." If you'd rather not deal with this, delete the four hardening lines.
- **Missed runs:** With `Persistent=true`, if the machine is off at 02:00, the backup runs at the next boot. Remove it if you only want runs at 02:00.
- **Timing:** `OnCalendar` uses the system's local time zone. `AccuracySec=1min` keeps the start within a minute of 02:00; the default lets it drift by up to a minute anyway. I left out `RandomizedDelaySec` because you asked for 02:00 exactly. Add it if several machines back up to the same target and you want to spread their start times.
- **Network:** If the backup only writes to local disk, you can drop the `Wants=` and `After=` lines on `network-online.target`.

Run `systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.*` to catch typos before you enable the timer. For an immediate test run, use `sudo systemctl start nightly-backup.service`, then read the output with `journalctl -u nightly-backup.service`.

If these units are for this workstation, keep the source copies in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/systemd/system/` and install them from there into `/etc`.
